question: to the Commission Gilles Pennelle (PfE), André Rougé (PfE) Subject:

The seed sector is of vital importance to the European Union’s food sovereignty and food security. France is Europe’s foremost producer (and the world’s second-largest exporter) of seeds of all kinds, including those used for arable and fodder crops. However, Ukrainian exports are increasingly undermining this sector’s competitiveness. The years 2017-2021 and 2022-2025 saw Ukraine’s seed exports increase their share of the EU market and the country’s total maize seed exports grow by 450 %, while French maize seed sales on the Ukrainian market fell by 40 % during the same period. Given the above, maintaining the EU’s seed production capacity becomes a food sovereignty and food security issue. 1.
Could the Commission share its assessment of Ukrainian seed production and export trends and their impact on the European and French seed sectors?
Will the Commission introduce measures to protect the internal market and ensure that the European seed sector can continue to compete with Ukrainian and, more generally, international stakeholders?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: Jean-Paul Garraud (PfE).
